explain.say: Reader, I married him. It may be the most famous line in English fiction, and notice who does the marrying: Jane. Charlotte Brontë published Jane Eyre in 1847 under the name Currer Bell. The timeline shows Jane's journey through five homes, from a locked room to a life she chooses.

explain.say: Start at Gateshead. Ten-year-old Jane is locked in the red-room, where her uncle died, and faints with terror. Then at Lowood, a harsh charity school, her gentle friend Helen Burns dies. Notice that Jane keeps speaking up for herself. What does a child who fights back tell you about the woman she will become?

explain.say: Here is Jane's web at Thornfield. She teaches little Adèle and falls for her moody employer, Rochester, telling him that though she is poor and plain, her soul is equal to his. But see the hidden link: Bertha, his first wife, locked in the attic. Why does Jane leave him, even though she loves him?

explain.say: Who is Bertha? On the left, the critics Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar read her as Jane's dark double, the rage Jane must hide. On the right, Gayatri Spivak and the novelist Jean Rhys see a Creole woman from Jamaica, silenced by empire. Which reading convinces you more?

At the end, Bertha sets Thornfield on fire and dies, and Rochester is blinded and loses a hand. Jane, now independent with her own inheritance, chooses to return to him at Ferndean. Wonderful. Challenge: is the ending a reward for Jane's strength, or does she win only once Rochester is humbled?

faq.q: What is the red-room in Jane Eyre?
faq.a: The room at Gateshead where Jane's uncle died. Her aunt, Mrs Reed, locks her in it as a punishment, and Jane, terrified she sees a ghost, faints. Many critics read it as the first of the novel's prisons for women.
asks: Red room meaning in Jane Eyre

faq.q: Who is the madwoman in the attic?
faq.a: Bertha Mason, Rochester's first wife, a Creole heiress from Jamaica whom he keeps locked on the third floor of Thornfield. Her existence stops Jane's wedding.
After the wedding is stopped, Rochester asks her to live with him anyway. Jane loves him but refuses to become his mistress, choosing her self-respect and principles over passion.
asks: Why does Jane run away from Thornfield?

faq.q: Why does Jane refuse St John Rivers?
faq.a: Her cousin St John wants her to marry him and serve as a missionary in India, but he does not love her. Jane will not marry without love, and she hears Rochester's voice calling her.

faq.q: What happens at the end of Jane Eyre?
faq.a: Jane returns to find Thornfield burned and Bertha dead. She marries the blinded Rochester at Ferndean, and he later regains some sight in one eye in time to see their first child.

facts: Jane Eyre was published in October 1847 under the pen name Currer Bell, with the subtitle An Autobiography.
Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar's feminist study The Madwoman in the Attic (1979) takes its title from Bertha Mason.
Jean Rhys's novel Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) retells Bertha's life before Thornfield.
